accepts, generated from the code that implements them. Read it when
you play a session, drive the JSONL stream, or write a verifier.

## Game commands

The grammar in every frame lists which of these are valid right now,
with one domain per argument. `move` offers every exit, walls included:
a blocked move still spends the turn and says why. Item commands offer
only items the command would work on.

| Command | What it does | Spends a turn | Events |
|---|---|---|---|
| `move <exit>` | Walk through an exit or a portal. | yes | `Moved`, `MoveBlocked`, `TurnAdvanced` |
| `look` | Look around again; the turn does not pass. | no | none |
| `wait` | Let one turn pass. | yes | `TurnAdvanced` |
| `take <item>` | Pick up an item lying where you stand. | yes | `ItemAcquired`, `TurnAdvanced` |
| `use <item>` | Use a carried consumable on yourself; offered only when it would help. | yes | `ItemUsed`, `Healed`, `TurnAdvanced` |
| `equip <item>` | Wear a carried item in its slot, replacing what was there. | yes | `ItemEquipped`, `TurnAdvanced` |

## Rejections

A refused command comes back as a rejection with a reason and a hint;
nothing changes and no turn passes.

| Reason | When | Hint |
|---|---|---|
| `no_such_exit` | `move` names something not on offer | "exits here: …", or "there are no exits here" |
| `not_here` | `take` names something not on offer | "you can take: …", or "there is nothing here to take" |
| `not_usable` | `use` names something not on offer | "you can use: …", or "nothing you carry would have an effect now" |
| `not_equippable` | `equip` names something not on offer | "you can equip: …", or "you are carrying nothing to equip" |
| `wrong_mode` | the verb exists, but not in the active mode | the verbs valid now |
| `unknown_verb` | no mode knows the verb | the verbs valid now |
| `unparsable` | the line is not a command at all (frontends) | the verbs valid now |
| `harness_disabled` | a meta command without `--harness` (frontends) | how to enable meta commands |
| `unknown_meta` | a `:` line that is not a meta command (frontends) | the meta commands' usage |

## Meta commands

Available with `--harness`; they never pass a turn.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `:query <path>` | answer one query path; see the paths below |
| `:query <path> --explain` | the same, with every contribution to a stat |
| `:seed` | the run's seed |
| `:frame` | the current frame, in the frontend's own form |
| `:frame --json` | the current frame as JSON |

## Query paths

`<id>` is an entity id and `<stat>` a stat name, such as
`player.stats.atk`.

| Path | Answer |
|---|---|
| `world.turn` | the current turn |
| `world.mode` | the active mode |
| `world.entities` | every entity id, sorted |
| `<id>.hp` | an actor's hp as [current, maximum] |
| `<id>.position` | where the entity stands, or null |
| `<id>.inventory` | the item ids it carries, in the order taken |
| `<id>.equipment` | its slots, as slot to item id |
| `<id>.stats.<stat>` | a stat's value; --explain adds every contribution |

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `no_such_entity` | no entity has that id |
| `no_such_path` | the path is not one of the paths above |
| `no_such_stat` | the entity neither has nor is modified in that stat |
